subject.title: [gateway] startup-migrations lease has no owner-liveness check — a crash-looping gateway can deadlock a second gateway indefinitely

question: Should the startup-migrations lease support automatic owner takeover, and what evidence is sufficient to declare an owner irrecoverably dead without allowing concurrent migrations?
rationale: The current gap affects availability, but aggressive takeover can violate the stronger checkpoint-integrity invariant, especially with shared state across hosts or PID reuse.

options.title: Bounded, identity-aware takeover
options.body: After reproducing the failure, add host, boot, process-start, and PID identity with same-host dead-owner takeover plus a hard maximum migration ownership window.

options.title: Progress-deadline only
options.body: Keep owners opaque and permit takeover only after a non-renewable maximum age or explicit lack-of-progress deadline, accepting slower recovery for stronger cross-host safety.

options.title: Unsupported shared-state topology
options.body: Keep TTL-only leases and document that independently supervised gateways must use isolated state directories, while improving the blocked-lease diagnostic.

recommendation.title: Bounded, identity-aware takeover
recommendation.body: After reproducing the failure, add host, boot, process-start, and PID identity with same-host dead-owner takeover plus a hard maximum migration ownership window.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the lease and checkpoint ownership model whose integrity and takeover contract must remain aligned.
